biography: Ricky Rudd, born under the Texas sun, practically grew up with a wrench in his hand. His father, a weekend dirt track racer, instilled a love for speed and competition early on. Ricky's childhood was filled with the roar of engines and the smell of burning rubber at the local short tracks. His defining moment came at age 16, when he took his father's battered pickup truck and won his first amateur race, a feat that earned him both bragging rights and a stern talking-to. Since then, he's been steadily climbing the ranks, quickly proving his defensive style can be frustrating to his opponents. Currently, he's a rising star in the Stock USA series, splitting his time between Stock USA Gen1 and Gen2 cars, hoping to prove he can make the jump to a full-time top-tier ride.
drivingStyle: Rudd is known for his intensely defensive driving style. He's a master of blocking and positioning, making it incredibly difficult for other drivers to pass him cleanly. While not the fastest driver on the track, he excels at tire management, often nursing his equipment to the end of a race while others fade. He thrives under pressure, rarely cracking when challenged, and isn't afraid to make a risky move to defend his position, even if it means making contact.

rivalries.reason: A heated rivalry stemming from a controversial late-race collision at Talladega, where Rudd was accused of intentionally wrecking Sanderson to secure a podium finish.
A battle of skill and strategy, Rudd and Thompson clash due to their opposing driving styles. Thompson's aggressive overtaking and Rudd's defensive blocking often lead to intense on-track battles.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of worn-out racing gloves for every race, claiming they bring him luck.
Before each race, he meticulously cleans and polishes his helmet, believing a shiny helmet makes him faster.
Refuses to eat anything red on race day, convinced it's bad luck.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about being the fastest, it's about being the smartest and outlasting the competition."
careerHighlight: Winning the Stock USA Gen2 Championship by a single point after a nail-biting final race at Daytona. He defended his position for the last ten laps against a charging field, showcasing his defensive prowess.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the Bristol Motor Speedway due to a mechanical failure, costing him a guaranteed win and a significant points lead in the Stock USA Gen1 series.
